name: nat_vent_active_indoor_in_band_guard_dormant__hvac_fan
description: [hvac_fan twin of golden 'nat_vent_active_indoor_in_band_guard_dormant'; Issue #1193] Regression guard: ceiling guard correctly dormant when nat-vent active and indoor within band
source: Issue #1193: hvac_fan twin of golden 'nat_vent_active_indoor_in_band_guard_dormant' (pre-#1140 version, fan configured). The golden is locked and now asserts the no-fan 'paused' result.

verdict.summary: [hvac_fan twin] When nat-vent is active and indoor is within comfort band (comfort_heat < indoor < comfort_cool), ceiling guard stays dormant
verdict.observed_behavior: nat_vent_active=True with indoor 73F within band [70F, 74F], outdoor 65F
verdict.expected_behavior: ceiling guard dormant, nat_vent continues, no HVAC intervention

events.note: Morning: indoor 72.5F, outdoor 65F (favorable for nat vent)
Window opens: outdoor 65F < indoor 72.5F, indoor > comfort_heat 70F, outdoor <= threshold 77F — nat vent activates
Same-instant refresh so the (zero-debounce) sensor timer fires: the harness only advances its virtual clock on event boundaries.

Mid-morning: indoor 73F still within comfort band [70F, 74F], outdoor 65F (still favorable). Nat vent continues to provide free cooling. Ceiling guard should remain dormant — this is correct behavior. A predicted_indoor curve crossing comfort_cool (74F) within the lead time is supplied so the guard has a breach to act on: without the dormancy rule it would escalate.

assertions.reason: [hvac_fan twin] Window opens with favorable conditions: outdoor 65F < indoor 72.5F, outdoor <= threshold 77F, indoor > comfort_heat 70F — nat vent activates

[hvac_fan twin] REGRESSION GUARD: temp_update with nat_vent_active and indoor 73F within band [70F, 74F] — ceiling guard dormant, nat vent continues. No HVAC change. This guards against broken ceiling guard logic that incorrectly fires when nat vent is already handling cooling.

notes: hvac_fan twin (Issue #1193): with the HVAC fan configured, an open window with usable outdoor air is ventilation (fan on), not a pause. This scenario pins the ventilation/exit/setback decision only; it deliberately does NOT assert the cool setpoint that production also arms during hvac_fan ventilation (nat_vent_ac_assist_armed), which is the rule-3 question tracked in #1142.

Issue #1193 revert-proofing: a thermal_model (confidence high) and a predicted_indoor curve that crosses comfort_cool within the lead time are supplied so the ODE ceiling guard is actually evaluated here; without them the guard returns MODEL_INELIGIBLE/NOT_APPLICABLE and a dormant-guard assertion passes vacuously. With the dormancy rule removed the guard escalates (clears nat-vent, commands cool) and the nat-vent assertion fails.
